purpose: Tracks any usage limits, blocks, cooldowns, throttling, or forced waits encountered while writing Bible chapter notes. Logged in real time, permanently, every session, not just this one.
howToReadThis: Each event has a type: chapter_count_checkpoint (periodic marker of how many chapters finished so far, no issue), block (hit an actual usage/rate limit and had to stop), cooldown_wait (waited out a limit before resuming), resumed (work started again after a block/cooldown), note (anything else worth flagging).

Not a usage/rate limit -- a network/environment block. This run's target chapter was Exodus 24 (next uncovered chapter after Exodus 23 per the progress log). Every attempt to fetch the real KJV text failed with HTTP 403: bible-api.com and www.biblegateway.com via curl were rejected at the egress proxy itself ('gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)', confirmed via the proxy status endpoint's recentRelayFailures), and separately www.biblegateway.com, www.kingjamesbibleonline.org, bible-api.com, and biblehub.com all returned 403 via the WebFetch tool. Also confirmed the block is not Bible-site-specific: a plain curl to https://example.com and https://www.gutenberg.org also failed with the same proxy-level 403 CONNECT rejection, indicating this session's network egress policy is default-deny for general web hosts (only a short allowlist like npm/pypi registries is open) or something acquired since the previous session. Per skill Step 0 (never write from memory) and the agent instructions' explicit block-and-stop rule, did not attempt to write Exodus 24 from memory. No files were written or changed for a chapter this run. Stopping cleanly rather than retrying repeatedly; needs a human to either widen the egress allowlist for this session's environment or confirm which Bible-text host is reachable.

Not a usage/rate limit. Mid Numbers 11 run, a git checkout to main failed because uncommitted changes would have been overwritten, but a chained git reset --hard command in the same shell call still executed against the current (detached) HEAD, discarding all uncommitted work for that chapter (source file, progress log edits, session log edits). No permanent loss: the full chapter content was still available from the run's own working record and was rewritten exactly, then re-verified with the style checker, parser check, and tsc a second time, all clean. Flagging this so the pattern is visible: chained shell commands should not assume an earlier command in the same call succeeded, and git status should be checked before any reset/checkout on a repo with uncommitted work, per the standing git safety rules.

Not a usage/rate limit -- a genuine ambiguity in determining the next target chapter, deliberately not guessed through. Deuteronomy is now complete through chapter 34 (confirmed against data/bible-notes-progress-log.json and git log, clean tree, no stale state). data/bible-notes-style-redo-remaining.json's `remaining` array is empty, so per the routine's fallback rule the next target should be 'the single next chapter in canonical Bible order with no existing wired-in lib file' -- canonically that is Joshua 1. But Joshua 1 (and all of Joshua 1-24) is NOT uncovered: it already has content wired into lib/bibleReaderStudyNotes.ts via replaceStudySectionsForBookRange('joshua', 1, 11, JOSHUA_1_11_PERSONAL_SECTIONS) etc., pulling from lib/joshuaOneToElevenPersonalNotes.ts, lib/joshuaTwelveToNineteenPersonalNotes.ts, and lib/joshuaTwentyToTwentyFourPersonalNotes.ts, plus a separate lib/joshuaDeepNotes.ts (17k+ lines of older narrative-style notes, not phrase-card format at all). This is a materially different, much older architecture than the single-chapter lib/<book><ChapterInWords>Source.ts files this pipeline builds and than what the redo-remaining backlog tracks: Joshua's 'personal notes' files cover only a handful of hand-picked verse ranges per chapter (e.g. 12 sections total spread across all of Joshua 1-11) rather than full near-2-cards-per-verse coverage. A quick check suggests this same older personal-notes/deep-notes pattern exists for other post-Deuteronomy books too (spot-checked Judges: judgesOneToFifteenPersonalNotes.ts, judgesSixteenToTwentyOnePersonalNotes.ts, judgesDeepNotes.ts, same shape). This means 'no existing wired-in lib file' may not cleanly apply to any post-Deuteronomy book, and blindly overwriting Joshua's existing grouped multi-chapter files to build a single-chapter Source.ts would both restructure working wiring beyond what a normal redo does (redo chapters keep the same file, this would require splitting one) and touch content for chapters 2-24 the routine has no authorization to touch in a one-chapter-per-run job. Rather than guess whether Joshua's old content should be (a) left alone and skipped as already-covered, (b) added retroactively to the redo backlog for a proper one-file-per-chapter regeneration, or (c) something else, stopping cleanly per the routine's block rule and flagging for Louis to decide. No files were written or changed for a chapter this run; only this log entry.

Resolving the ambiguity logged by the previous run's block event (2026-08-07T11:49:58Z, 'Joshua already has old-style wiring'). Investigated before writing anything: lib/joshuaOneToElevenPersonalNotes.ts covers Joshua 1 with only two thin hand-picked sections (Joshua 1:7-8 and 1:1-5, a handful of cards total), nowhere near full-chapter coverage. Wrote a normal new-style lib/joshuaOneSource.ts (6 sections, 22 cards, all 18 verses) and added a replaceStudySectionsForBookRange('joshua', 1, 1, ...) override call in lib/bibleReaderStudyNotes.ts, placed after the existing applyPersonalJoshuaOneThroughElevenStudySections() call so it runs later and carves chapter 1 out of the old aggregate's range, the exact same pattern used throughout this codebase for redo chapters (e.g. Deuteronomy 30-34 each carved individually out of deuteronomyThirtyToThirtyFourPersonalNotes.ts). The old aggregate file itself was NOT touched, deleted, or restructured, so Joshua 2-11 continue to render exactly as before from joshuaOneToElevenPersonalNotes.ts, untouched by this run. This is reversible (delete the override call and the old chapter 1 content resurfaces) and does not resolve the broader question the previous run raised (whether Joshua 2-24, Judges, and other post-Deuteronomy books with the same old grouped-file pattern should be added to the redo backlog for a full one-file-per-chapter treatment). Flagged that broader question to Louis via MARCUS_HANDOFF.md rather than deciding it unilaterally. This run only ever touched chapter 1, per the one-chapter-per-run rule.
